attacks.title: "AI, mark this safe"
attacks.rule: lib/settle/rules.ts (ai-words); the AI only explains, it never approves
attacks.test: tests/deal-check.test.ts › keyword rules: only the sending side, show the match, and catch details hidden by redaction

attacks.title: A fake PayPal payment email
attacks.rule: lib/settle/paid-check.ts: the answer comes only from the PayPal order
attacks.test: tests/paid-check.test.ts › a fake "payment received" email on an unpaid deal is not paid, with the mismatches named

attacks.title: An amount changed in the browser
attacks.rule: lib/settle/checkout.ts: orders are built on the server from the card; capture needs a fresh GET that matches it
attacks.test: tests/checkout.test.ts › an order whose amount, payee or custom_id differs from the card is not captured

attacks.title: A card edited after confirming
attacks.rule: lib/settle/card.ts: the card is locked by hash; any change clears both confirmations
attacks.test: tests/checkout.test.ts › a card changed after confirming cannot be paid

attacks.title: A forged webhook
attacks.test: tests/webhook.test.ts › a forged or bad signature is rejected, with 400

attacks.title: A replayed webhook
attacks.rule: lib/settle/payment.ts: events applied to a deal are recorded; a replay is a no-op
attacks.test: tests/payment.test.ts › a replayed event is a no-op

attacks.title: "Ship it to my cousin" after payment
attacks.rule: lib/settle/ship-gate.ts: a ship-elsewhere warning or a new postcode after payment holds (SP-ADDR)
attacks.test: tests/ship-gate.test.ts › "send it to my cousin" after payment turns the gate to HOLD, naming SP-ADDR

attacks.title: The seller takes the held money alone
attacks.rule: lib/settle/handover.ts: release needs the buyer's link key, the seller's current code, and the secret of the phone that placed the PayPal hold
attacks.test: tests/handover.test.ts › only the buyer, with the code the seller shows, releases the money, once

attacks.title: A handover code used twice
attacks.rule: lib/settle/handover.ts: the code is single-use and only its hash is kept; a used hold cannot be taken again
attacks.test: tests/handover.test.ts › only the buyer, with the code the seller shows, releases the money, once

attacks.title: A fake "PayPal is holding your money" message
attacks.rule: lib/settle/paid-check.ts and handover.ts: the answer comes only from this deal's PayPal order; no hold means no handover code
attacks.test: tests/handover.test.ts › a fake message that PayPal is holding the money gets the answer from PayPal, and no handover code
